items.text: Diagram of implications between classes of morphisms
closed immersion $\Rightarrow$ finite $\Rightarrow$ projective $\Rightarrow$ quasi-projective; finite $\Rightarrow$ integral $\Rightarrow$ affine; integral $\Rightarrow$ universally closed.
finite = integral + finite type; integral = affine + universally closed (subtler).
projective $\Rightarrow$ proper $\Rightarrow$ separated and universally closed; closed immersion $\Rightarrow$ quasi-compact immersion $\Rightarrow$ quasi-affine.
affine $\Rightarrow$ quasi-affine; quasi-affine of finite type $\Rightarrow$ quasi-projective.
Finite $=$ proper with finite fibres (the converse is subtle; EGA).
Ample sheaves, corrected: the absolute case
$X$ coherent, $\mathcal L$ invertible, $S_n=\Gamma(X,\mathcal L^{\otimes n})$, $f\in S_n$, $X_f=\{x: f(x)\neq0\}$; $X_f\cap X_g=X_{fg}$.
Equivalent conditions on $\mathcal L$:
(a) the $X_f$ ($f\in S_n$, $n$ variable) form a basis of the topology; (a$'$) the affine $X_f$ form a basis.
\text{(b) every quasi-coherent }\mathcal F\ \text{of finite type: }\exists\,n_0,\ \forall n\ge n_0,\ \ \mathcal F(n)=\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes n}\ \text{generated by its sections}
\mathcal O_X^m\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal F(n)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\mathcal O_X^m(-n)\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal F
(b$'$) same for quasi-coherent ideals $\mathcal F\subset\mathcal O_X$ of finite type.
Over an affine $Y$: sufficient (and necessary when $f$ is of finite type) that some $\mathcal L^{\otimes n}$, $n>0$, (equivalently all $n\ge n_0$) is very ample relative to $Y$.
Definition. $\mathcal L$ is ample if these conditions hold (not « a power is very ample »).
The relative case
$\mathcal L$ ample relative to $Y$: $Y=\bigcup Y_i$ affine with $\mathcal L|_{X_i}$ ample and $X_i$ coherent; then $f$ is coherent and $X$ separated over $Y$. Stable under base change.
\text{Relative form of (b), }Y\text{ quasi-compact:}\quad f^*f_*\mathcal F(n)\longrightarrow\mathcal F(n)\ \text{surjective for }n\gg0
Some positive power of $\mathcal L$ very ample $\Rightarrow$ $\mathcal L$ ample; the converse for $f$ of finite type and $Y$ quasi-compact.
Correct statement for composition
$Z$ quasi-compact, $\mathcal L$ on $X$ ample (resp. very ample) relative to $f$, $\mathcal M$ on $Y$ ample (resp. very ample) relative to $g$:
\exists\,n_0:\ \ \mathcal L\otimes f^*\mathcal M^{\otimes n}\ \text{is ample (resp. very ample) relative to }g\circ f\quad\forall n\ge n_0

Idea (very ample case): $X\subset\mathbf P^n_Y$, $Y\subset\mathbf P^m_Z$, hence $X\subset\mathbf P^n_Z\times_Z\mathbf P^m_Z\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^{(n+1)(m+1)-1}_Z$ (Segre), inducing $\mathcal L\otimes f^*\mathcal M$.

\mathcal E\otimes\mathcal M^{\otimes n}\ \text{quotient of a free sheaf }(\mathcal M\ \text{ample}),\qquad \mathbf P(\mathcal E)\simeq\mathbf P(\mathcal E\otimes\mathcal I),\ \ \mathcal O_{\mathbf P(\mathcal E\otimes\mathcal I)}(1)=\mathcal O_{\mathbf P(\mathcal E)}(1)\otimes\mathcal I
Quasi-projective and projective are not local on the base; stable under composition only for quasi-compact schemes.
Quasi-affine schemes
$X$ quasi-affine: isomorphic to a quasi-compact open subscheme of an affine scheme (then coherent).
A=\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X),\qquad j\colon X\to\operatorname{Spec}A\ \text{(universal map to an affine scheme)}
